paragraphs.en: When Liam McGee departed as president of Bank of America in August, his explanation was surprisingly straight up. Rather than cloaking his exit in the usual vague excuses, he came right out and said he was leaving “to pursue my goal of running a company.” Broadcasting his ambition was “very much my decision,” McGee says. Within two weeks, he was talking for the first time with the board of Hartford Financial Services Group, which named him CEO and chairman on September 29.
paragraphs.zh: 利亚姆·麦基八月份辞去美国银行总裁一职时，给出的解释坦率得令人惊讶。他没有用惯常的含糊借口掩饰离职原因，而是直截了当地说，离开是“为了追求我执掌一家公司的目标”。麦基说，公开自己的抱负“完全是我自己的决定”。不到两周，他就首次与哈特福德金融服务集团董事会进行了交谈，后者于9月29日任命他为首席执行官兼董事长。

paragraphs.en: McGee says leaving without a position lined up gave him time to reflect on what kind of company he wanted to run. It also sent a clear message to the outside world about his aspirations. And McGee isn’t alone. In recent weeks the No.2 executives at Avon and American Express quit with the explanation that they were looking for a CEO post. As boards scrutinize succession plans in response to shareholder pressure, executives who don’t get the nod also may wish to move on. A turbulent business environment also has senior managers cautious of letting vague pronouncements cloud their reputations.
paragraphs.zh: 麦基说，在尚未找好下一份工作时离职，使他有时间思考自己究竟想管理怎样的公司，同时也向外界清楚地传达了自己的志向。这样做的并非只有麦基。最近几周，雅芳和美国运通的二把手都辞职了，给出的解释都是希望寻找首席执行官职位。随着董事会为回应股东压力而仔细审查接班计划，那些未获认可的高管，也可能希望另谋出路。动荡的商业环境还使高层管理者格外谨慎，不愿让模糊的声明影响自己的声誉。

paragraphs.en: As the first signs of recovery begin to take hold, deputy chiefs may be more willing to make the jump without a net. In the third quarter, CEO turnover was down 23% from a year ago as nervous boards stuck with the leaders they had, according to Liberum Research. As the economy picks up, opportunities will abound for aspiring leaders.
paragraphs.zh: 随着最初的复苏迹象开始稳固，副手们可能更愿意在没有后路的情况下跳槽。利伯鲁姆研究公司的数据显示，第三季度首席执行官更替数量同比下降了23%，因为心怀不安的董事会仍然留用了现有领导者。随着经济回升，胸怀抱负的领导者将拥有大量机会。

paragraphs.en: The decision to quit a senior position to look for a better one is unconventional. For years executives and headhunters have adhered to the rule that the most attractive CEO candidates are the ones who must be poached. Says Korn/Ferry senior partner Dennis Carey: “I can’t think of a single search I’ve done where a board has not instructed me to look at sitting CEOs first.”
paragraphs.zh: 辞去高层职位，去寻找一个更好的职位，这种决定并不符合惯例。多年来，高管和猎头一直遵循一个原则：最有吸引力的首席执行官候选人，是那些必须从别处挖来的人。光辉国际高级合伙人丹尼斯·凯里说：“我做过的招聘中，想不出有哪一次董事会没有要求我优先考虑在任的首席执行官。”

paragraphs.en: Those who jumped without a job haven’t always landed in top positions quickly. Ellen Marram quit as chief of Tropicana a decade ago, saying she wanted to be a CEO. It was a year before she became head of a tiny Internet-based commodities exchange. Robert Willumstad left Citigroup in 2005 with ambitions to be a CEO. He finally took that post at a major financial institution three years later.
paragraphs.zh: 那些没有找好新工作就离职的人，并不总能很快坐上最高职位。十年前，埃伦·马拉姆辞去纯果乐负责人的职务时，表示希望成为首席执行官。过了一年，她才出任一家小型网络商品交易所的负责人。罗伯特·威勒姆斯塔德于2005年离开花旗集团，也怀着成为首席执行官的抱负。直到三年后，他才终于在一家大型金融机构得到这个职位。

paragraphs.en: Many recruiters say the old disgrace is fading for top performers. The financial crisis has made it more acceptable to be between jobs or to leave a bad one. “The traditional rule was it’s safer to stay where you are, but that’s been fundamentally inverted,” says one headhunter. “The people who’ve been hurt the worst are those who’ve stayed too long.”
paragraphs.zh: 许多招聘人员表示，对于表现出色的人而言，以往附着在这种做法上的不光彩色彩正在消退。金融危机使暂时待业或离开一份糟糕的工作，变得更容易被接受。一位猎头说：“传统的原则是，留在原处更安全，但现在情况发生了根本性逆转。受伤最重的，恰恰是那些待得太久的人。”
